problem.text: The FP32-input gated-activation kernel converted activation(x)*y directly to FP16, allowing large products to overflow the output representation.

reasoning.text: Clamp the converted half2 pair before storing it. This preserves FP32 activation and multiplication while bounding the FP16 result; it does not clamp inputs or intermediate arithmetic.

impact.text: The change covers both SiLU and GELU specializations with FP32 inputs. The FP16-input kernel and PyTorch-based non-gated MLP activations remain unchanged, so the commit message is broader than the implementation.

source_notes.text: The FP32-activation ancestor entry records the mixed-precision output contract, incompatible in-place FP32 callers and an omitted odd-element tail.

Current source retains the GatedMLP destination mismatch and odd-element tail. Unlike the earlier entry's account, the parent BlockSparseMLP ordinary path now supplies a separate half destination when needed; its fused path also supplies a half destination.

The inspected discussions concern different failures: “TypeError with presence penalty” reports argument incompatibility, while “humaneval.py: fix top_k type, remove rep_p, add qwen3” discusses evaluation, penalty-kernel NaNs and prompting. Neither establishes the motivation for this activation clamp.

limitations: No CUDA build, kernel execution, model evaluation or performance measurement was performed.
The scalar check models binary16 rounding and saturation, not CUDA intrinsic execution or NaN handling.
Whole-tree literal caller searches do not establish the behavior of dynamic or external callers.

chapters.title: Saturate FP32 gated-activation outputs at the FP16 store

claims.text: act_mul_kernel_f loads float2 pairs, applies SiLU or the tanh-based GELU approximation per lane, multiplies by the corresponding y lanes, then rounds to half2. The new helper applies an upper bound followed by a lower bound to that converted pair before the store.

The bounds ±65504 are binary16's finite extrema: (2−2^-10)×2^15 = 65504. A standard-library scalar model retained ordinary rounded values and saturated modeled overflow: 65000 became 64992, while ±70000 became ±65504 after conversion and clamping.

Placing the clamp after conversion allows the existing half2 min/max operations to bound overflowed output lanes without widening the destination. This trades extreme-value magnitude for a bounded representation; it does not recover precision lost during conversion or establish that earlier arithmetic was finite.

silu_mul and gelu_mul dispatch on x.dtype(), require matching input dtypes and always require a half destination. Their FP32 branches share the changed kernel; the half-input branches still store __hmul2 directly without this clamp.

Whole-tree searches locate the exported operations in GatedMLP and BlockSparseMLP. BlockSparseMLP's ordinary expert path allocates half a when interm_dtype is not half, and its fused path uses half interm_a. These paths can reach the clamp with FP32 gate/up results. GatedMLP instead passes u as both input and destination, so FP32 u fails validation before reaching it.

findings.description: GatedMLP retains an in-place destination incompatible with the FP32-input activation contract.
findings.trigger: GatedMLP.forward receives FP32 gate/up projection results.
findings.expected_behavior: Supply a half activation destination so the supported FP32-input kernel can run.
findings.actual_behavior: activation_fn_call(g, u, u) supplies FP32 z; the wrapper rejects z before launching the newly clamped kernel. Both BlockSparseMLP activation paths prepare half destinations instead.

verification.description: Compared whole-tree activation caller matches, destination preparation and unchanged wrapper checks.
verification.limits: Conditional on FP32 projection results; no model execution.

findings.description: The clamp does not repair the inherited omission of an odd final element.
findings.trigger: Call either exported activation with otherwise suitable buffers and an odd element count.
findings.expected_behavior: Write activation(x)*y for every output element.
findings.actual_behavior: Both kernels process only numel/2 complete pairs. The final destination element remains untouched; wrappers have neither an evenness check nor a scalar tail.

verification.description: Enumerated the inspected launch and pair-index arithmetic. Lengths 1, 3, 129 and 513 each omitted their final index; 128 and 512 were fully covered.
verification.limits: Index model only, not kernel execution. Exported calls expose the case; this does not establish that normal padded model workloads produce odd lengths.

annotation.summary: Bounds FP32-input SiLU/GELU gated products at the FP16 store using ±65504; half-input arithmetic and inherited caller/tail limitations remain unchanged.
